claim.title: Grokking probability increases with L1 regularisation
claim.statement: For the D-dimensional uniform ball model, the probability of achieving zero test error (grokking probability) is significantly higher with L1 regularisation ($\lambda_1 > 0$) compared to L2 regularisation ($\lambda_1 = 0$), especially for small class separations $\epsilon$.
claim.test_plan: Run multiple trials of the D-dimensional uniform ball model (e.g., $D=10, N=20, \epsilon=1.01$). For each trial, train the model with $\lambda_1=0, \lambda_2=0.1$ and separately with $\lambda_1=0.1, \lambda_2=0.1$. Count the fraction of trials that reach zero test error (grok). Pass if the grokking probability with $\lambda_1 > 0$ is at least 2x higher than with $\lambda_1 = 0$, or if the probability with $\lambda_1 > 0$ is $> 0.5$ while $\lambda_1 = 0$ is $< 0.1$ (consistent with Fig 8 trends and text in 3.3.2).
claim.evidence_in_paper: Section 3.3.2: 'In the case $\lambda_1 > 0$, the grokking probability can increase even above 90%... In contrast, in the $\lambda_1 = 0$ case, the grokking probability becomes exponentially small with D.'
claim.success_criterion: The empirical grokking probability with L1 regularisation is strictly greater than with L2 regularisation (specifically, $P_{\text{grok}}(\lambda_1>0) > P_{\text{grok}}(\lambda_1=0)$) for the specified parameters.
